profile.headline: Senior Backend Engineer | AWS Microservices, Java & Python | Platforms at Scale
profile.summary:
I build and operate backend platforms on AWS that other teams depend on every day. At Nike, I’ve spent most of the last seven years in Marketing Technology—first owning cloud services for globalization (store, translate, and serve localized content), and for the past two years on digital assets (images, video, and related metadata) used across consumer experiences.

On the globalization side, I architected a platform now used by 100+ internal teams, holding 60,000+ text phrases in up to 35 languages. That work included Java/Python microservices on EC2, cross-account migrations with no planned downtime, performance tuning (including a 5× improvement on a critical download path), SLA definition with load testing (Gatling), and observability (Splunk, SignalFx). I also helped deliver content personalization integrated with Adobe Target, with measurable revenue impact for the business.

More recently I’ve focused on digital asset management within  Marketing Technology backend services for how creative assets are stored, discovered, and delivered. I contributed to an initiative that replaced an embedded third-party DAM (projected ~$3M annual savings), and I helped plan and execute the deprecation of a significant enterprise SaaS tool—migrating capabilities onto internal platforms, coordinating integrators, and keeping production stable through the transition.

I am a top-down, outside-in thinker, beginning any big challenge with a research phase where I am relentless in my pursuit to understand as many of the requirements, the platform seams, the timeline, and all other relevant constraints.  With the arrival of AI-assisted coding, I've found this approach to be even more crucial to its success, since the coding effort is diminishing while the need for maintainability, robustness, extensibility, cost and performance is becoming even more important.

I care about clear ownership, maintainable services, and smooth handoffs—I’ve transitioned platforms to teams in Europe and India without disrupting users. My stack is Java (8–23), Python, TypeScript/Node.js, AWS (Lambda, EC2, ECS, Kinesis, SQS/SNS, DynamoDB, S3, CloudFormation/Terraform), and solid CI/CD and testing practices.

What I’m looking for: Senior backend or platform engineering (and the right Tech Lead or hands-on leadership role) at companies where engineering is central to the product—including health, insurance, and enterprise software.  I'm based in the Portland area and am open to hybrid work.  I would be happy to connect with engineers, hiring managers, and recruiters working on similar problems.

positions.description:

• Past two years: backend engineering for digital assets (images, video, metadata) in MarTech—ingestion, management, search, and delivery to downstream consumers.

• Backend work on DAM modernization replacing an embedded third-party system—~$3M/year projected savings; Java/Python microservices on AWS.

• Key role in deprecating two major enterprise SaaS platforms—migration paths, replacement services, integrator coordination, stable cutovers.

• Content personalization via Adobe Target—tens of millions of dollars in business-attributed revenue impact.

• 5× performance improvement on a critical download path; zero-downtime migration of a 5-service platform across AWS accounts (Commerce → Waffle).

positions.title: Back-End Software Developer
positions.description:
Summary:  Back-end development of data management utilities for the company’s flagship website.
	Wrote Java code for new capabilities (75%) and legacy bug-fixes (25%).
	Developed interfaces for four third-party API’s to gather data and then serve it on a dashboard.
	Implemented two interfaces that used web-hooks and tracking pixels.
	Wrote and deployed six micro-services, configured and deployed on AWS Lambda and EC2.

positions.title: Consulting Engineer and Program Manager
positions.description: Leading the development of a new energy management appliance for a young company.  Management of contractors and vendors doing electrical and firmware development, assembly and testing, and serving as key customer contact.

positions.title: Consulting Program Manager and Engineer
positions.description: Provided support necessary for the pursuit of developing new testing tools for the chip industry.  This included managing vendors for the necessary electrical, mechanical and software components and ensuring their smooth integration.  I was also the primary contact with the customer, both for weekly updates as well as providing on-site delivery and support of the equipment.
